picks.why: Best crown-to-brim balance and soft felt shading, and it sits centred. 1 has an oversized crown and 2 sits off-centre to the left.
Only candidate. It reads at once as a cowboy boot, with believable proportions and a spur that belongs to the object.
The central round emblem makes it read instantly as a sheriff's badge. 1 is a blank star with an awkward pin, and 3's gold-on-silver star reads more like a generic award.
Only candidate. The coil and loop read clearly as a lasso, and the fence rail is a modest, plausible prop.
Tall, true proportions and real spines. 2's round knobs and flared pot rim look like a toy.
Clean four-wheel wagon, centred, with a restrained canvas cover. 1 has oversized wheels and an odd A-frame tongue, and 2 sits off-centre with an added hitch ring.
Most believable saddle shape, sitting centred and framed by both fence posts. 1 has a stray shadow floating on the background, and 2 is off-centre and cropped by the fence.
Simplest staging: pot and small log fire with no pile of rocks, soft wear and a gentle dent. 1 and 3 add stones, and 1 has a harder dent and the fire overlapping the pot.
Most restrained and readable: simple false front, batwing doors and few windows, matching the real cards' lower detail. 1 is tall and monochrome, and 2 adds interior lamps and extra busy detail.
Coherent, centred locomotive with a believable stack-to-boiler ratio. 1's smokestack is oversized, and 2 sits off-centre with the headlamp tacked onto the stack.
